source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: You see two model implementations with similar processing steps, but one uses much larger parameter arrays. What conclusion is supported?

options.text: Larger parameter arrays must contain more hand-written answer rules
options.feedback: Parameters are learned numerical values. Their larger size does not mean programmers wrote a separate rule for every possible answer.

options.text: Larger parameter arrays make context unnecessary for interpretation
options.feedback: Context still influences representations through attention. Parameter size does not remove the value of relevant task information.

options.text: Similar operations can work with very different learned models
options.feedback: The notes separate the broad algorithm from parameter size and values. Similar processing steps do not make the models identical.

options.text: Similar processing steps require the same parameter values
options.feedback: The algorithm specifies operations, while training determines many values. Matching broad steps does not establish identical learned numbers.
